240	## 2. Colors
241	
242	One warm charcoal ramp, one violet signal, and two status hues reserved for truth-telling.
243	
244	### Primary
245	- **Dusk Lavender** (`focus-accent`): the single "you are here" signal. Used for the 4px bar on the focused row, the active message bar in the reader, focus outlines, and the highlighted command. It never fills an area and never decorates.
246	
247	### Secondary
248	- **Orchid Dot** (`unread-marker`): only for the 5px unread dot in the row gutter. It is pinker than Dusk Lavender so that unread and focus never read as the same signal.
249	
250	### Neutral
251	- **Warm Charcoal** (`surface`): the list, rail and header plane. Everything sits on it.
252	- **Deep Umber** (`surface-contact`): the contact pane and utility drawers. It is one step darker, so context reads as secondary to the list.
253	- **Lifted Charcoal** (`surface-raised`): utility chips, overlays and inputs.
254	- **Focus Stone** (`focus-fill`): the focused-row and active-message fill, and the highlighted command item.
255	- **Inkwell** (`rail-well`): the pill behind the rail's navigation glyphs.
256	- **Rail Pebble** (`rail-button`): the circular rail action button.
257	- **Paper White** (`text-primary`): sender, subject, active tab, contact name and email, labels.
258	- **Ash** (`text-secondary`): snippet, date, group caption, contact threads, counts.
259	- **Smoke** (`text-tertiary`): inactive split tabs.
260	- **Graphite** (`icon-muted`): every resting glyph (row actions, compose, search, hamburger, footer icons, attachment). Hover and focus raise glyphs to Paper White. Graphite is 2.75:1 on Focus Stone and 3.79:1 on Lifted Charcoal, so it never carries meaningful text, or a glyph that must be read, on a focus fill or the composer fill; Ash does that job there.
261	- **Seam** (`divider`): the 1px vertical separators between rail, list and contact pane, and the drawer's leading edge; also the 1px border of utility chips, fields and floating panels. Never between rows.
262	- **Rule** (`rule`): a quieter 1px structure line inside a pane, used only in the reader and inside drawers. Never in the list.
263	
264	### Status
265	- **Amber Notice** (`warning`): pending, outcome unknown, local-only, expired-undo and partial states.
266	- **Coral Fault** (`danger`): confirmed failures and command errors.
267	
268	### Named Rules
269	**The One Signal Rule.** Dusk Lavender appears at most once per screen, on the current row or message. If two violet things are visible, one of them is wrong.
270	
271	**The Seams-Only Rule.** Dividers separate panes, never rows. Rows are separated by rhythm alone.
272	
273	**The Status-Is-Sacred Rule.** Amber and coral are never used decoratively, and a status is never shown only as a tint: every status carries words.

275	## 3. Typography
276	
277	**Body Font:** system-ui (with -apple-system, sans-serif)
278	**Label/Mono Font:** ui-monospace, for plain-text message bodies only
279	
280	**Character:** One local system sans in two weights carries the whole UI. Hierarchy comes from weight (600 vs 400) and tone (Paper White vs Ash), not size. The browsing shell uses just two sizes.
281	
282	### Hierarchy
283	- **Headline** (400, 1rem / 16px, 1.25): split tabs and the contact name. This is the only large text in the shell.
284	- **Title** (600, 0.75rem / 12px, 1.35): sender names, contact email, section labels ("Mail"), footer labels, notice labels.
285	- **Body** (400, 0.75rem / 12px, 1.35): subject (Paper White), snippet and threads (Ash), date-group captions (Ash).
286	- **Label** (400, 0.75rem / 12px, tabular numerals): dates ("8:00 AM", "6 NOV" with an uppercase month) and counts in status text.
287	- **Mono** and the other steps are CSS tokens: `--type-headline`, `--type-body`, `--type-count`, `--type-mono`, `--weight-regular`, `--weight-strong` (`src/assets/style.css`). Use the tokens, never a literal size.
288	
289	### Dates
290	Row and reader dates are one fixed product format, not a locale format. They depend only on the instant, the current time and the viewer's time zone (`src/lib/browsing-dates.ts`). Month group captions ("October 2026") still follow the locale.
291	- **Row, today:** the time, 12-hour, no leading zero: "8:00 AM", "12:05 PM".
292	- **Row, earlier this calendar year:** day and month: "6 NOV". The DOM text is "6 Nov"; CSS uppercases it, so screen readers hear a word, not letters.
293	- **Row, any other year (past or future):** day, month and four-digit year: "9 JAN 2025". The day is kept for precision, and a two-digit year would read as another day.
294	- **Unknown or unparsable:** "Unknown" in the row, "Unknown date" in full form. Never blank.
295	- **Full form** (reader message times, the row date's hover title): "Thu 9 Jan 2025, 6:29 PM". The same 12-hour clock as the row.
296	- Every rendered date is a `<time>` with a normalized ISO `datetime` when the timestamp parses.
297	- **Count** (400, 0.6875rem / 11px): split-tab counts, set 4px after the tab label.
298	- **Mono** (400, 0.85rem, 1.45): the current plain-text message body in the reader.
299	
300	Sizes are rem so the 16px and 20px root-font layouts in `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts` still scale. Row and header heights are min-heights in px. The 12px row size is measured from the capture: system-ui glyph metrics point to 11.5–12px.
301	
302	### Named Rules
303	**The Two-Size Rule.** The browsing shell uses 16px and 12px only (11px for counts). A third size in the list needs a written reason.
304	
305	**The No-Caps-Caption Rule.** No uppercase letter-spaced captions in the browsing shell. Date groups and pane headings are title case. Uppercase is allowed only for the month in compact dates.

308	
309	The browsing shell is flat. Depth comes from tonal layering: Warm Charcoal for the plane, Deep Umber for context, Focus Stone for the current row, Inkwell for the rail well. No shadows sit on rows, panes, the header or the rail. Shadows appear only on surfaces that truly float above the shell and cover it.

312	- **Drawer cast** (`box-shadow: -8px 0 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`): the right-edge utility drawer (Activity, Account, Drafts).
313	- **Popover lift** (`box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`): the compact row-actions disclosure panel.
314	- **Overlay lift** (`box-shadow: 0 16px 64px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.53)`): the command palette and navigator, over a `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.53)` backdrop (`--overlay-lift`, `--overlay-backdrop`).
315	
316	### Named Rules
317	**The Flat-Shell Rule.** If something in the rail, header, list or contact pane casts a shadow, remove it. Shadows mean "this covers the shell", nothing else.

343	### Contact Pane
344	- **Style:** 272px on Deep Umber, with a 1px Seam on its left and a 24px inset. No visible caption heading (it stays for assistive tech).
345	- **Content:** the name in Headline on the tab line; the email in Title on the first list line; copy glyphs in each line's trailing slot, revealed on hover or focus; a section label (Title with a 16px glyph) followed by recent threads (Body, Ash, ellipsis, 24px pitch); exact known data only, never invented enrichment.
346	- **Footer:** none. Superhuman's footer toolbar has no counterpart with real actions here; the utilities live in the rail (Parity gap 9).
347	
348	### Buttons
349	- **Ghost (browsing shell, the default):** transparent, Paper White text or a Graphite glyph, 4px radius, `4px 8px` (24px tall). Text ghosts in the dock bars (selection actions, Undo, Load more) carry the Title weight. Hover lifts a text ghost to Lifted Charcoal and a glyph to Paper White; press is Focus Stone; disabled is 0.45 opacity. The focus ring is a 2px Dusk Lavender outline at a 1px offset.
350	- **Utility (drawers, the attachment chooser, recovery banners):** a Lifted Charcoal fill with a 1px Seam border, 4px radius, `3px 8px` (24px tall); hover is Focus Stone. This is the only bordered button.
351	- **Specificity:** the defaults are `:where()` rules, so a component class (split tab, rail item, row action, contact line) always wins without `!important`.
352	
353	### Command Overlay
354	- **Style:** a Lifted Charcoal panel, 10px radius, 576px max width, no border, Overlay lift, 15vh from the top. There is no caption: the placeholder and the dialog's accessible name say whether it is Commands or Destinations. The 38px query (16px Headline) sits on Deep Umber with a 1px Dusk Lavender border; it always owns keyboard focus, so that border is its focus indicator. Items are 36px rows of 12px Body with a 16px Graphite glyph that turns Paper White when highlighted. The highlighted item gets a Focus Stone fill plus a 3px Dusk Lavender left bar. Disabled items are Smoke, with their reason in Ash. Shortcuts are `kbd` in Ash on Deep Umber, compact ("G then E", timing in the tooltip). The hint line sits under a 1px Seam.
355	- **Groups (palette only):** Conversation, Selection, View, Go to, each a sentence-case 11px Ash label, no rule, no caps. The Destinations navigator is one group and stays unlabelled. Items are searched by label, aliases (undo → revert, archive → done, snooze → remind) and their exact bound key; the empty state says what did not match ("No command matches “…”.").
356	- **Glyphs:** `CommandGlyph.vue` reuses RowGlyph, HeaderGlyph and PaneGlyph where the idea already has a glyph, and draws the few palette-only ones (open, undo, selection, splits, filter, switch account) on the same 16px grid.
357	- **Keys:** a quiet list under the commands for bound keys that are not commands (J/K, X, Shift+J/K, Left). They are text rows, never options: no highlight, no pointer, never executed. Filtered by the same query.
358	
359	### Composer (reply and new message)
360	- **Shell:** Lifted Charcoal with a 1px Seam border, docked at the bottom of the reader pane (6px radius, capped at 60% of the pane) or, for a new message with no reader, the in-flow card (10px radius). Never a modal.
361	- **Heading line:** the title on the left (Title weight, `Reply draft to Ada Fixture` or `New Message`) and the one status line on the right (Body, Ash when settled, Amber Notice otherwise).
362	- **Rows:** a 3.5rem Ash label column, then an input with a quiet Seam underline at rest (full Seam border on hover); the reply shows only `To  <name>` as a button until the user asks for more. Body: at least six lines, grows, bordered like a field.
363	- **Footer:** primary `Save and close` (Focus Stone, Title weight) with an Ash `Esc` hint, quiet Ash `Discard…`. The only buttons besides the confirm dialogs and retry actions. No Send.
364	
365	### Reader Message Disclosures
366	- **Status line:** one Ash line under the subject for the read state (plus `Read-only`); standing guarantees live in its title and hidden text. Exceptions stay as Amber Notice lines.
367	- **Quote and signature:** Ash reading-face blocks after the prose; the quote is behind a ghost toggle. **Attachments:** a plain list of 24px lines under the body, ghost `Save` per file.
368	
369	### Inputs / Fields
370	- **Style:** a Lifted Charcoal fill, a 1px Seam border, 4px radius, inherited font.
371	- **Focus:** the border shifts to Dusk Lavender, doubled by a 1px inner outline so the ring reads at 12px. No glow.
372	- **Placeholder:** Smoke (4.76:1 on Lifted Charcoal).
373	
374	### In-flow Notices (Action notice, Selection bar, coverage and recovery)
375	- **Style:** borderless lines in normal flow, with text on the 50px content inset, in Body type with 6px block padding. Status words use Amber Notice or Coral Fault. Undo shows its `kbd` hint in Ash. They never overlay rows and never auto-hide a failure.
376	- **Bottom dock (transient lines):** the Selection bar, the Action notice and the command-error alert sit in a dock at the bottom of the list column, below the list, never above it. Showing or hiding them never moves a row. The dock reserves one 36px line and grows upward into the list viewport; the focused row is kept whole when the viewport shrinks. Its lines are whole-pixel (16px line height, 24px buttons). This is the honest, in-flow form of Superhuman's bottom undo toast: no float, no shadow, nothing covered.
377	- **Above the list (static lines):** Starred/Done coverage notes and the draft-close recovery banner, which belong to the destination or to a pending recovery rather than to the last keystroke.
378	
379	## 6. Do's and Don'ts
380	
381	### Do:
382	- **Do** keep rows at exactly 36px with 12px type, and separate them by rhythm alone.
383	- **Do** align split tabs, sender names, date captions, notices and the bottom dock to the single 50px content inset.
384	- **Do** use Dusk Lavender (#bba5ed) only for the current row or message, and the focus ring.
385	- **Do** show every pending, partial, failed and outcome-unknown state in words, in Amber Notice or Coral Fault, where the user is already looking.
386	- **Do** align the contact pane to the list: the name on the tab line, the email on the first-row line.
387	- **Do** ship glyphs as local inline SVG with an accessible name. No icon fonts and no CDN.
388	- **Do** name each action once, in sentence case, on every surface (row glyph, selection bar, reader, Activity, action notice, palette): "Mark done" / "Mark not done" (E / Shift+E), "Mark read" / "Mark unread", "Star" / "Unstar". Counted forms keep the verb: "Mark 3 done". Destinations keep their proper names (Inbox, Done, Starred, Trash, Provider mail, Activity) after "Go to". "Archive" is the provider-side effect, never a label; it survives only as a palette search alias.
389	- **Do** treat Superhuman's browsing look as the visual and interaction reference. Close look parity is the goal (PRODUCT.md).
390	
391	### Don't:
392	- **Don't** draw dividers between rows or under the header. Seams separate panes only.
393	- **Don't** use uppercase letter-spaced captions in the browsing shell.
394	- **Don't** add Gmail-web clutter: toolbars of rarely-used icons, or chrome competing with content.
395	- **Don't** add "AI magic" chrome: sparkle icons, or generated summaries presented as fact.
396	- **Don't** build a Superhuman feature-parity clone. Copy the browsing look, not Superhuman's product scope.
397	- **Don't** use generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics: card grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration.
398	- **Don't** show optimistic UI that lies: no "Done" toast before the provider confirms, and no silent retry of an ambiguous send.
399	- **Don't** put shadows on anything in the rail, header, list or contact pane.
400	- **Don't** use Graphite for text or meaningful glyphs on Focus Stone or on the composer's Lifted Charcoal fill. Use Ash.
401	- **Don't** repeat a standing guarantee as a paragraph on every open. State it once, in a status line with the detail in its title; only exceptions interrupt.
402	- **Don't** introduce a third type size in the list, or use off-palette hex values (the old command-overlay violets are the cautionary example).
403	- **Don't** load remote fonts, images or CDN assets.

# Critique run 1: reader + reply/compose

Method: single-agent, code-and-test verification only. Nothing was rendered (no Chrome on this VM, no screenshots), so every visual claim below is read from CSS and templates, not measured. The prior whole-app review scored this area 22/40 and ranked it next (attention 8/10). Each of its findings was re-checked against the code and tests; verdicts are marked CONFIRMED, PARTLY WRONG or REJECTED. Inbox list and search were critiqued earlier and are out of scope.

## Heuristics 23/40
| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | "Saved locally / Saving locally…" exists but sits beside a 3-line disclaimer and is amber at rest |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 2 | Raw `conversationId · messageId` in the composer; "N bytes"; "Prepare reply" |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc flushes and closes, Discard confirms; no keyboard way to start a reply |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | Two reply glyphs; quoted block in mono while the body is proportional; reply form unlike every other reply UI |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Fields disabled while a reply is unprepared; conflict and recovery paths are solid |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | No reply entry in the palette or key hints; the shortcut list says nothing about reply |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 2 | Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z); replying is mouse-only |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 1 | Up to six caveat paragraphs above the thread; a 4-field form plus 3-line note plus ID line above 3 lines of typing room |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry save, Save as new, Reload saved are explicit and honest |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | A permanent disclaimer is doing the job a status line and a title should do |
| | **Total** | **23/40** | Acceptable |

Why 23 and not 22: `useDrafts.statusLabel` already yields an honest settled state ("Saved locally"), so the fix for the disclaimer is to promote that line, not invent a new one.

## Findings: verification

### 1. No reply shortcut — CONFIRMED, P1
`grep` finds no `r` binding anywhere in `App.vue`'s `onKeydown`, and `browsing-actions.ts` has no `reply` action. `prepareReply` (App.vue:1587) is reached only from `ReaderView` emitting `prepareReply`, from two controls: the header glyph `data-test="prepare-reply"` (ReaderView:710-720) and a per-message glyph on the active latest message (ReaderView:848-862). Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z/C); replying is the one step that needs the pointer, which breaks "keyboard first" in the middle of the triage loop.
Safety already holds for a new key: the dispatcher returns for editable targets and IME (`isComposing`/`keyCode 229`, App.vue:1867-1869), returns early while a composer owns keys (App.vue:1866), and `actionShortcutBlocked` lets message toggles through but blocks other buttons. Reply must stay reader-only: the list holds no loaded message, so a list-level R would have to open, load and then reply, which is new scope. The source stays the displayed latest message (never the focused one), and the key must be unavailable for Cached Trash (`browsingOnly`), blocked replies (retained snapshot, incomplete, header mismatch), non-ready state and an open drawer.
Fix: add `reply` to `browsingActions` (label unchanged: "Prepare reply", shortcut R, so existing accessible names stay), `actionGroupOf`, `actionAliases` (respond, answer, write back), `actionAvailable`, `executeAction`, and the key handler; surface "R" in the header glyph title and palette; drive the reader's button titles from `actionLabel('reply')`.

### 2. Reply composer is a form — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore` renders four always-visible labelled fields (To, Cc, Subject, Body) in a 2-column grid (`.composer-fields`, style.css:1819), with a body that is `min-height: 8rem` (5rem when docked, style.css:2070). The core already pre-fills To and `Re: …` Subject for a reply (asserted in `reply-composer.component.test.ts:88-90`), so showing them as empty-looking boxes asks the user to re-read fields they never need to touch. Cc is optional and never filled for a reply. The new-message card needs To and Subject visible (they start empty) but Cc is rarely used.
Fix: reply surface gets a one-line recipient row ("To  Ada Fixture"), Cc and Subject behind a quiet "Cc / Subject" disclosure, and the body is the dominant, auto-focused field. New message keeps To and Subject visible and puts Cc on demand. The To row must never misrepresent the field: show the display name only while To is still the default sender mailbox, and the raw text once edited. Existing `data-test` hooks stay on the inputs; tests that read Cc or Subject reveal them first.
Quoted source: `.reply-quoted` is `--font-mono` at `--type-mono` (0.85rem), larger than the 12px shell and the proportional reading face above it (style.css, ReplyComposer.vue:154-165). Switch to the UI face at the body size in `--text-secondary` (4.99:1 on Focus Stone, ≥ 7:1 on `surface-raised`), keep the 2px rule and pre-wrap, keep it read-only and out of `bodyText`.

### 3. Permanent disclaimer and raw IDs — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore.vue:90-93` prints three lines on every open, every surface: "Local-only plain text. No Send action exists. Recipient text is stored raw… Cc is optional; Bcc, reply-all, quoted text, and rich text are not supported." It also contradicts the UI: it says quoted text is unsupported directly above a quoted block. `ReplyComposer.vue:110-112` and `DraftsPanel.vue:148` print `Reply source is fixed: <conversationId> · <messageId>`: opaque provider IDs a person cannot act on. The settled status line is `.draft-status`, which is colored `--warning` even when everything is fine, so amber at rest dilutes "local-only" as a real warning.
Fix: one line, "Saved locally · not sent" (settled, Ash) / "Saving locally…" / "Save not confirmed" (Amber Notice), with the detail ("Local plain-text draft. Nothing is sent. Recipients are stored as typed and not validated. Bcc, reply-all and rich text are not supported.") in the `title` and a visually hidden description for assistive tech. Drop the ID line from every surface; keep the IDs only as `data-source-*` attributes that tests can read (no visible text). The drawer's own `draft-local-note` in `DraftsPanel` stays (a different surface), but the editor core no longer duplicates it.
Footer: today it is `Close editor` / `Discard…` as equal ghosts with no key hint. Close already flushes (saves) first, and Esc does the same. Fix: primary "Save and close" (Esc kbd hint, Focus Stone fill, Title weight), secondary "Discard…" as an Ash ghost. Honesty is unchanged: the button still waits on the flush and the editor stays open with the error if it fails. No Send, ever.

### 4. Reader header caveats — CONFIRMED, P1
ReaderView:778-816 stacks up to six paragraphs under the subject before the first message: star line, reply-blocked, retained snapshot, one of three read-only/no-auto-read variants, unsupported-or-incomplete, pending. Two are standing statements repeated on every open: "Opening this conversation does not change read state; use an explicit read control" (Gmail with actions) and "Read-only Gmail view: messages are never marked as read. Opening this conversation does not change read state." (Gmail read-only), plus the Cached Trash text. The rest are real exceptions and should stay.
Fix: one muted status line in the existing meta row ("Unread" / "Read-only · Unread"), with the full sentence in its `title` and as visually hidden text, so the guarantee stays discoverable without repeating on screen. Keep every exception inline and amber: reply blocked, retained snapshot, unsupported/incomplete, pending, star attention. Keep the `reader-readonly` / `reader-no-auto-read` hooks on the status line. The Trash notice drops its "Opening does not change read state." sentence and keeps what Trash actually restricts.

### 5. Quoted blocks and signatures force monospace — CONFIRMED, P2
`bodyNeedsMonospace` returns true on the first line matching `^ {0,3}>`, so every reply-chain message renders entirely in mono (message-body-format.ts); two consecutive 4-space-indented lines (signatures, lists) do the same. The quoted tail is also what makes most real threads long.
Fix: split a plain-text body deterministically into prose, an optional signature (after a `-- ` delimiter, only when the tail is short) and an optional trailing quote (an "On … wrote:" attribution line, or a contiguous run of `>` lines to the end). Decide monospace from the prose part only, render signature and quote in the reading face in Ash, and put the quote behind a "Show quoted text" disclosure (per message, kept in the visit state so it survives J/K round trips). Still literal text via interpolation, the `>` characters are never rewritten, nothing is dropped, and interleaved (inline) quotes stay in place and keep the mono rule. The collapsed-row snippet uses the prose part so a message that is mostly quote does not preview as `>`.

### 6. Attachments are second-class — CONFIRMED, P2
`ReaderView` never references `Message.hasAttachment` (a known-true/false/unknown DTO field). Attachments are reachable only through the Cmd+O chooser (a modal). `AttachmentChooser.vue:91` prints `{{ file.size }} bytes` (a 4,812,333-byte file reads as a 7-digit number), and a 230-character paragraph sits above the list (lines 84-85). Its two lists share the same flat style.
Fix: inline attachment rows under the expanded body of each message that has files: name, human size ("27 B", "4.6 MB"), a Save button, and a Cancel while transferring, with the same pending/status/error semantics as the chooser (extract the save/cancel state into one shared composable, no second implementation). Where `hasAttachment === true` but no descriptor is cached, say so plainly ("Attachment not available offline: sync to fetch"); where it is unknown, show nothing (never inferred). Over-5-MiB files say "Over 5 MiB limit". The chooser keeps its role for links and the full list, loses the raw byte counts, and its intro paragraph shrinks to one line with the rest in a `title`/muted note ("Download only. Files save inert with a .download suffix.").

### 7. Loading state and type system — PARTLY WRONG
- Loading: the bare "Loading conversation…" shows only when the shell has no row identity (`loadingIdentity` null: Activity/Reminders/recent-mail entry). From the list the reader already shows the row's subject, sender and date first (ReaderView:735-742, tested). The holding state during J/K keeps the previous conversation on screen. Low value, P3. Small fix only: give the bare line `role="status"`; keep the exact text the smooth-navigation test pins.
- Collapsed sender column — REJECTED. `flex: 0 0 11em` at 12px is 132px, exactly the list's sender column. Its Ash/regular weight is deliberate: only the active message is Paper White/strong, which keeps the One Signal rule. Making it strong would erase that distinction.
- Uppercased date — REJECTED. `.message-time` uppercases the month exactly as `.row-time` does (style.css:1151 vs 1526), and DESIGN.md "Dates" specifies this ("6 Nov" in the DOM, "6 NOV" on screen). The reader already matches the list.
- Reply composer height — CONFIRMED. `.reply-composer { max-height: 45% }` with a 5rem textarea and a 4-field header, a 3-line note and an ID line leaves roughly three lines to type in, and the whole composer scrolls internally. The compact layout in findings 2 and 3 fixes this: the body gets a `min-height` of at least 6 lines and grows, the shell scrolls only when the thread and composer genuinely do not fit.

## Cross-cutting: contrast
Computed from the tokens (WCAG relative luminance): Graphite `#8e8a87` is 4.30:1 on Warm Charcoal, 3.79:1 on Lifted Charcoal `#33312e` and 2.75:1 on Focus Stone `#474644` (under the 3:1 non-text floor). Ash `#c0bcb6` is 7.79 / 6.86 / 4.99:1 on the same three. Smoke `#a09c9a` is 5.41 / 4.76 / 3.46:1. Nothing new in this area may use Graphite for a meaningful glyph or text on Focus Stone, and Graphite text on Lifted Charcoal (3.79:1) is below the 4.5:1 text floor. Current offenders in scope: the `.message-details summary` label ("Details", Graphite text on the active message's `surface-raised` fill, 3.79:1) and the `.message-reply` glyph on the same fill (passes 3:1 as a glyph, but text-sized hints do not). New composer glyphs and hints use Ash.

## Remaining priority issues (after this pass)
- P2 — The inline reply composer and the new-message card still scroll internally when the thread is very short. A true minimum thread viewport needs a rendered pass.
- P3 — The two reply glyphs (header and per-message) overlap in function; after R lands, the per-message glyph could go. Left in place: removing a visible control is a separate decision.
- P3 — Recipient autocompletion and validation do not exist by design (raw text, drafts local-only).

## Rendered check (added after implementation)
The fixture-only browser preview (Vite dev server, 1280×800, T3 browser) was driven through: open conversation → R → reply composer (body focused, `To  Ada Fixture`, status line, footer) → Cc / Subject → expand first message (inline attachment row, `27 B · text/plain`, Save) → Esc (focus back on the active message) → C (new-message card) → 20px root font. One defect only visible when rendered: empty Cc/To/Subject inputs had a transparent border, so the row looked like plain text; fixed with a Seam underline at rest. Seen but out of scope: the contact pane's "Composing to …" line pushes the contact name 33px off the tab line while a draft is open (ContactPane, untouched); closing the docked new-message card leaves focus on `<body>` (reply composer now restores it).
Not rendered: the quote toggle (no fixture message has a quote), Gmail-mode status line, Cached Trash, blocked-reply states; those are covered by component tests only.

## Not verified
Contrast numbers are computed from tokens, not sampled from pixels. Native/WKWebView is not exercised. Contrast numbers are computed from the tokens, not sampled from pixels. Real-Chrome journeys (`reader.rendered.test.ts`) are opt-in on `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME` and cannot run on this VM.

# Critique run 1: reader + reply/compose

Method: single-agent, code-and-test verification only. Nothing was rendered (no Chrome on this VM, no screenshots), so every visual claim below is read from CSS and templates, not measured. The prior whole-app review scored this area 22/40 and ranked it next (attention 8/10). Each of its findings was re-checked against the code and tests; verdicts are marked CONFIRMED, PARTLY WRONG or REJECTED. Inbox list and search were critiqued earlier and are out of scope.

## Heuristics 23/40
| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | "Saved locally / Saving locally…" exists but sits beside a 3-line disclaimer and is amber at rest |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 2 | Raw `conversationId · messageId` in the composer; "N bytes"; "Prepare reply" |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc flushes and closes, Discard confirms; no keyboard way to start a reply |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | Two reply glyphs; quoted block in mono while the body is proportional; reply form unlike every other reply UI |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Fields disabled while a reply is unprepared; conflict and recovery paths are solid |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | No reply entry in the palette or key hints; the shortcut list says nothing about reply |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 2 | Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z); replying is mouse-only |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 1 | Up to six caveat paragraphs above the thread; a 4-field form plus 3-line note plus ID line above 3 lines of typing room |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry save, Save as new, Reload saved are explicit and honest |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | A permanent disclaimer is doing the job a status line and a title should do |
| | **Total** | **23/40** | Acceptable |

Why 23 and not 22: `useDrafts.statusLabel` already yields an honest settled state ("Saved locally"), so the fix for the disclaimer is to promote that line, not invent a new one.

## Findings: verification

### 1. No reply shortcut — CONFIRMED, P1
`grep` finds no `r` binding anywhere in `App.vue`'s `onKeydown`, and `browsing-actions.ts` has no `reply` action. `prepareReply` (App.vue:1587) is reached only from `ReaderView` emitting `prepareReply`, from two controls: the header glyph `data-test="prepare-reply"` (ReaderView:710-720) and a per-message glyph on the active latest message (ReaderView:848-862). Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z/C); replying is the one step that needs the pointer, which breaks "keyboard first" in the middle of the triage loop.
Safety already holds for a new key: the dispatcher returns for editable targets and IME (`isComposing`/`keyCode 229`, App.vue:1867-1869), returns early while a composer owns keys (App.vue:1866), and `actionShortcutBlocked` lets message toggles through but blocks other buttons. Reply must stay reader-only: the list holds no loaded message, so a list-level R would have to open, load and then reply, which is new scope. The source stays the displayed latest message (never the focused one), and the key must be unavailable for Cached Trash (`browsingOnly`), blocked replies (retained snapshot, incomplete, header mismatch), non-ready state and an open drawer.
Fix: add `reply` to `browsingActions` (label unchanged: "Prepare reply", shortcut R, so existing accessible names stay), `actionGroupOf`, `actionAliases` (respond, answer, write back), `actionAvailable`, `executeAction`, and the key handler; surface "R" in the header glyph title and palette; drive the reader's button titles from `actionLabel('reply')`.

### 2. Reply composer is a form — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore` renders four always-visible labelled fields (To, Cc, Subject, Body) in a 2-column grid (`.composer-fields`, style.css:1819), with a body that is `min-height: 8rem` (5rem when docked, style.css:2070). The core already pre-fills To and `Re: …` Subject for a reply (asserted in `reply-composer.component.test.ts:88-90`), so showing them as empty-looking boxes asks the user to re-read fields they never need to touch. Cc is optional and never filled for a reply. The new-message card needs To and Subject visible (they start empty) but Cc is rarely used.
Fix: reply surface gets a one-line recipient row ("To  Ada Fixture"), Cc and Subject behind a quiet "Cc / Subject" disclosure, and the body is the dominant, auto-focused field. New message keeps To and Subject visible and puts Cc on demand. The To row must never misrepresent the field: show the display name only while To is still the default sender mailbox, and the raw text once edited. Existing `data-test` hooks stay on the inputs; tests that read Cc or Subject reveal them first.
Quoted source: `.reply-quoted` is `--font-mono` at `--type-mono` (0.85rem), larger than the 12px shell and the proportional reading face above it (style.css, ReplyComposer.vue:154-165). Switch to the UI face at the body size in `--text-secondary` (4.99:1 on Focus Stone, ≥ 7:1 on `surface-raised`), keep the 2px rule and pre-wrap, keep it read-only and out of `bodyText`.

### 3. Permanent disclaimer and raw IDs — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore.vue:90-93` prints three lines on every open, every surface: "Local-only plain text. No Send action exists. Recipient text is stored raw… Cc is optional; Bcc, reply-all, quoted text, and rich text are not supported." It also contradicts the UI: it says quoted text is unsupported directly above a quoted block. `ReplyComposer.vue:110-112` and `DraftsPanel.vue:148` print `Reply source is fixed: <conversationId> · <messageId>`: opaque provider IDs a person cannot act on. The settled status line is `.draft-status`, which is colored `--warning` even when everything is fine, so amber at rest dilutes "local-only" as a real warning.
Fix: one line, "Saved locally · not sent" (settled, Ash) / "Saving locally…" / "Save not confirmed" (Amber Notice), with the detail ("Local plain-text draft. Nothing is sent. Recipients are stored as typed and not validated. Bcc, reply-all and rich text are not supported.") in the `title` and a visually hidden description for assistive tech. Drop the ID line from every surface; keep the IDs only as `data-source-*` attributes that tests can read (no visible text). The drawer's own `draft-local-note` in `DraftsPanel` stays (a different surface), but the editor core no longer duplicates it.
Footer: today it is `Close editor` / `Discard…` as equal ghosts with no key hint. Close already flushes (saves) first, and Esc does the same. Fix: primary "Save and close" (Esc kbd hint, Focus Stone fill, Title weight), secondary "Discard…" as an Ash ghost. Honesty is unchanged: the button still waits on the flush and the editor stays open with the error if it fails. No Send, ever.

### 4. Reader header caveats — CONFIRMED, P1
ReaderView:778-816 stacks up to six paragraphs under the subject before the first message: star line, reply-blocked, retained snapshot, one of three read-only/no-auto-read variants, unsupported-or-incomplete, pending. Two are standing statements repeated on every open: "Opening this conversation does not change read state; use an explicit read control" (Gmail with actions) and "Read-only Gmail view: messages are never marked as read. Opening this conversation does not change read state." (Gmail read-only), plus the Cached Trash text. The rest are real exceptions and should stay.
Fix: one muted status line in the existing meta row ("Unread" / "Read-only · Unread"), with the full sentence in its `title` and as visually hidden text, so the guarantee stays discoverable without repeating on screen. Keep every exception inline and amber: reply blocked, retained snapshot, unsupported/incomplete, pending, star attention. Keep the `reader-readonly` / `reader-no-auto-read` hooks on the status line. The Trash notice drops its "Opening does not change read state." sentence and keeps what Trash actually restricts.

### 5. Quoted blocks and signatures force monospace — CONFIRMED, P2
`bodyNeedsMonospace` returns true on the first line matching `^ {0,3}>`, so every reply-chain message renders entirely in mono (message-body-format.ts); two consecutive 4-space-indented lines (signatures, lists) do the same. The quoted tail is also what makes most real threads long.
Fix: split a plain-text body deterministically into prose, an optional signature (after a `-- ` delimiter, only when the tail is short) and an optional trailing quote (an "On … wrote:" attribution line, or a contiguous run of `>` lines to the end). Decide monospace from the prose part only, render signature and quote in the reading face in Ash, and put the quote behind a "Show quoted text" disclosure (per message, kept in the visit state so it survives J/K round trips). Still literal text via interpolation, the `>` characters are never rewritten, nothing is dropped, and interleaved (inline) quotes stay in place and keep the mono rule. The collapsed-row snippet uses the prose part so a message that is mostly quote does not preview as `>`.

### 6. Attachments are second-class — CONFIRMED, P2
`ReaderView` never references `Message.hasAttachment` (a known-true/false/unknown DTO field). Attachments are reachable only through the Cmd+O chooser (a modal). `AttachmentChooser.vue:91` prints `{{ file.size }} bytes` (a 4,812,333-byte file reads as a 7-digit number), and a 230-character paragraph sits above the list (lines 84-85). Its two lists share the same flat style.
Fix: inline attachment rows under the expanded body of each message that has files: name, human size ("27 B", "4.6 MB"), a Save button, and a Cancel while transferring, with the same pending/status/error semantics as the chooser (extract the save/cancel state into one shared composable, no second implementation). Where `hasAttachment === true` but no descriptor is cached, say so plainly ("Attachment not available offline: sync to fetch"); where it is unknown, show nothing (never inferred). Over-5-MiB files say "Over 5 MiB limit". The chooser keeps its role for links and the full list, loses the raw byte counts, and its intro paragraph shrinks to one line with the rest in a `title`/muted note ("Download only. Files save inert with a .download suffix.").

### 7. Loading state and type system — PARTLY WRONG
- Loading: the bare "Loading conversation…" shows only when the shell has no row identity (`loadingIdentity` null: Activity/Reminders/recent-mail entry). From the list the reader already shows the row's subject, sender and date first (ReaderView:735-742, tested). The holding state during J/K keeps the previous conversation on screen. Low value, P3. Small fix only: give the bare line `role="status"`; keep the exact text the smooth-navigation test pins.
- Collapsed sender column — REJECTED. `flex: 0 0 11em` at 12px is 132px, exactly the list's sender column. Its Ash/regular weight is deliberate: only the active message is Paper White/strong, which keeps the One Signal rule. Making it strong would erase that distinction.
- Uppercased date — REJECTED. `.message-time` uppercases the month exactly as `.row-time` does (style.css:1151 vs 1526), and DESIGN.md "Dates" specifies this ("6 Nov" in the DOM, "6 NOV" on screen). The reader already matches the list.
- Reply composer height — CONFIRMED. `.reply-composer { max-height: 45% }` with a 5rem textarea and a 4-field header, a 3-line note and an ID line leaves roughly three lines to type in, and the whole composer scrolls internally. The compact layout in findings 2 and 3 fixes this: the body gets a `min-height` of at least 6 lines and grows, the shell scrolls only when the thread and composer genuinely do not fit.

## Cross-cutting: contrast
Computed from the tokens (WCAG relative luminance): Graphite `#8e8a87` is 4.30:1 on Warm Charcoal, 3.79:1 on Lifted Charcoal `#33312e` and 2.75:1 on Focus Stone `#474644` (under the 3:1 non-text floor). Ash `#c0bcb6` is 7.79 / 6.86 / 4.99:1 on the same three. Smoke `#a09c9a` is 5.41 / 4.76 / 3.46:1. Nothing new in this area may use Graphite for a meaningful glyph or text on Focus Stone, and Graphite text on Lifted Charcoal (3.79:1) is below the 4.5:1 text floor. Current offenders in scope: the `.message-details summary` label ("Details", Graphite text on the active message's `surface-raised` fill, 3.79:1) and the `.message-reply` glyph on the same fill (passes 3:1 as a glyph, but text-sized hints do not). New composer glyphs and hints use Ash.

## Remaining priority issues (after this pass)
- P2 — The inline reply composer and the new-message card still scroll internally when the thread is very short. A true minimum thread viewport needs a rendered pass.
- P3 — The two reply glyphs (header and per-message) overlap in function; after R lands, the per-message glyph could go. Left in place: removing a visible control is a separate decision.
- P3 — Recipient autocompletion and validation do not exist by design (raw text, drafts local-only).

## Rendered check (added after implementation)
The fixture-only browser preview (Vite dev server, 1280×800, T3 browser) was driven through: open conversation → R → reply composer (body focused, `To  Ada Fixture`, status line, footer) → Cc / Subject → expand first message (inline attachment row, `27 B · text/plain`, Save) → Esc (focus back on the active message) → C (new-message card) → 20px root font. One defect only visible when rendered: empty Cc/To/Subject inputs had a transparent border, so the row looked like plain text; fixed with a Seam underline at rest. Seen but out of scope: the contact pane's "Composing to …" line pushes the contact name 33px off the tab line while a draft is open (ContactPane, untouched); closing the docked new-message card leaves focus on `<body>` (reply composer now restores it).
Not rendered: the quote toggle (no fixture message has a quote), Gmail-mode status line, Cached Trash, blocked-reply states; those are covered by component tests only.

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

## Layout

| Path | Owner |
|---|---|
| `crates/mail-core/` | Rust DTOs, fixture core, Gmail provider/auth/cache/sync/actions, SQLite, profile locks |
| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |
| `src-tauri/` | Thin Tauri 2 shell: typed mail/draft/close commands, `mailbox_changed` and `drafts_changed` hints, fixture/Gmail profile selection and lifecycle |
| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto
`b4972ee`, the UX-06/07/08 contracts are preserved but not extended by this
increment. See [the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

## Layout

| Path | Owner |
|---|---|
| `crates/mail-core/` | Rust DTOs, fixture core, Gmail provider/auth/cache/sync/actions, SQLite, profile locks |
| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |
| `src-tauri/` | Thin Tauri 2 shell: typed mail/draft/close commands, `mailbox_changed` and `drafts_changed` hints, fixture/Gmail profile selection and lifecycle |
| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto
`b4972ee`, the UX-06/07/08 contracts are preserved but not extended by this
increment. See [the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)

Use when asked to implement a scoped change in this repo. Delegates implementation to the local persona-feature-engineer agent. --- # Implement Implement the requested change in Email OS. The request can be a task description, an approved plan, or a path to a repository document with a specific item to implement. No ticket service is required. Usage: `/skill:implement ` All repository paths below are relative to the repository root. The local persona definition is `.pi/agents/persona-feature-engineer.md` from the repository root. Runtimes that mirror these documents through symlinks keep this path authoritative; follow the target, not the mirror location. ## 1. Establish the task - Read the request and referenced documents. Identify the goal, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and affected code. - If the request names a broad document, ask which item to implement. Do not treat every proposed feature in that document as approved work. - Ask for clarification if a product, architecture, data migration, or scope decision is missing. Do not invent requirements. - Inspect the working-tree status. Preserve pre-existing edits and keep one writer per checkout. ## 2. Gather repository context Use local code and documentation, not external wiki or code-graph services: - `README.md` for the project entry points and document map. - `docs/development.md` for setup, commands, profile isolation, and validation gates. - `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` for accepted first-build scope. - The relevant slice or UX contract under `docs/`, and the relevant section of `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` or `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` for browsing work. - `ARCHITECTURE.md` only as a proposal, not as an inventory of implemented behavior. The PRD and older research do not authorize scope expansion. - Current code and tests to confirm actual behavior. Escalate material conflicts between the task, accepted contracts, and implementation. Find the affected seam: - `crates/mail-core/`: Rust mail core, DTOs, SQLite, Gmail auth/provider/cache/sync/actions. - `src/` and `tests/`: Vue 3/TypeScript UI, IPC adapter, and frontend tests. - `src-tauri/`: thin Tauri 2 native shell and command/event bridge. - `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts`: generated wire contract. Never edit it by hand; change the Rust DTOs and run `mise run gen:ts`. Follow existing conventions and any applicable project instructions. Do not invent a separate coding-standard source. ## 3. The count line stays as a `role=status` fragment ("12 cached · total unknown") because the count is data, not a disclaimer. The empty state keeps "This does not mean your Gmail Trash is empty." Failure stays a Coral `role=alert` with Retry. - Existing test pins: text contains "not your complete Gmail Trash"; `button[data-id]` rows; focus returns to the `data-id` row on Esc; the alert contains the error kind; the empty text contains "does not mean your Gmail Trash is empty". These contracts survive. ### 3. Drafts: a two-column grid inside a 460px drawer — CONFIRMED, P1 `.drafts-pane` is `grid-template-columns: minmax(190px, .7fr) minmax(0, 2fr)` (style.css ~1752) with a collapse only at `max-width: 760px`, but the drawer is `min(460px, 92vw)` wide, so the media query never fires at desktop widths. The local-only paragraph, a "Draft to {name}" line and the editor's own `h2` repeat what the drawer header and the editor status line already say. The raw "Reply source is fixed: " line is already gone (PR #29 moved it into hidden `data-source-*` attributes), so that sub-claim is **stale, not actionable**. Fix: one column. The list is the default view; opening a draft or New draft replaces the list with the editor (`DraftEditorCore` untouched), with a quiet `Back to drafts` ghost and Esc: the editor's existing Esc already runs the protected flush-and-close, which hides the editor and returns the list, and a second Esc closes the drawer. Rows are 36px: recipient (Title), subject (Body, Ash if empty-state placeholder), date trailing (`FullDate` compact). Revision appears only on a conflict (the `status` string already says "Conflict — edits preserved"); the revision lives in the title. One Ash line: "Local to this device · never sent". Reschedule and Cancel become quiet ghost text buttons ("Reschedule", "Cancel reminder"); the "restore original inbox messages" sentence and the failed-phase explanation move to titles (the failed explanation stays inline: it is an exception). - Picker: preset buttons (Later today, Tomorrow, Next week, Someday) compute a real RFC3339 string with a numeric offset in the viewer's time zone and fill the same `due` ref; the typed field sits behind `Custom`. `put` payloads are unchanged, so exact-retry and revision semantics are untouched. Raw conversation / message IDs leave the picker (subject instead; IDs in a title). - Existing test pins: `input[type="text"]` (now behind Custom), "removing" text, `nav button` tabs, `Refresh reminders` / `Retry exact request` / `Reschedule` button texts, the `timezone offset` error. These are updated, not weakened. ### 5. Duplicate headings and nested landmarks — CONFIRMED, P2 `App.vue` renders `
` with `

` and then each panel adds its own landmark and sometimes its own title: Activity `
` + `

Activity

`; Drafts `
` + `

Drafts

`; Reminders `
`; Cached Trash `
`. So "Activity" is announced twice (and "Operation activity" a third time) and an `aside` complementary landmark sits inside a region. `drawerTitles` also has long labels ("Provider mail — read only", "Cached Trash — read only") that are used as both the visible h2 and the accessible name, so the visible title is wordy. Fix: the drawer owns the region name and the single visible h2. Panels become plain `div`s (no landmark, no heading that repeats the title). Account / Provider mail keep their markup (out of scope) but must still get a drawer header. Visible titles shorten ("Activity", "Drafts", "Reminders", "Cached Trash"); the long names stay as the region's `aria-label` where tests pin them (`Local drafts`, `Provider mail — read only`). The drawer-header close button stays. ### 6. Row borders and bordered boxes — PARTLY WRONG (documented exception, but it conflicts with the rule it sits under) DESIGN.md ("Palette deltas", gap 10) explicitly keeps `rule` for "inside drawers (Activity and draft rows, group detail, Account panel, Reminders fieldset)", with the stated reason "so those surfaces keep their tone until a reader reference is captured". So the borders are not undocumented drift, but they are a carried-over stopgap and they contradict "Seams-Only Rule: dividers separate panes, never rows". `.activity-row`, `.draft-row` have `border-bottom: var(--rule)`; `.activity-group-detail` and `.discard-confirm` are boxed; the reminders `fieldset` is boxed. Decision: the redesigned rows are 36px rhythm rows with no borders (Activity rows, draft rows, group detail members, reminder rows); the group detail loses its box and indents by rhythm; the reminders fieldset loses its border. `rule` stays only for the reader and the Account panel (out of scope here), and for the composer's own structure (footer rule, discard confirm: untouched, owned by PR #29). DESIGN.md gap 10 is updated to say so. ### 7. No keyboard model in any drawer — CONFIRMED, P1 No panel has a key handler, a roving tabindex or row-level focus. With a drawer open App returns early for everything but Escape (`if (drawer.value ...) return;`, App.vue ~1937), so J/K and arrows are free to be owned by the panel. Escape closes the drawer through the window handler and returns focus to the rail toggle (`closeDrawer`), which already works from any drawer element. Fix: one shared composable (`useDrawerRows`) used by all four panels: a container handler for ArrowDown / ArrowUp / J / K / Home / End, Enter activates the row's primary action (rows are real buttons or carry one), roving `tabindex` (focused row 0, others -1, first row when none), `data-drawer-row` marker, and `aria-current` free. It ignores editable targets, IME composition, modifier keys, `repeat` where an action would double-fire, and non-row buttons (trailing actions keep native Enter/Space). Cached Trash's remembered focus (`state.focusedId`) feeds the roving index. Esc stays with App (closes the drawer; in the drafts editor the editor's own Esc flushes and returns to the list first). ### 8. Off-scale spacing and the missing 50px inset — CONFIRMED, P2 `.utility-drawer { padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem }`; row gaps 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.35 / 0.4 / 0.5 / 0.8 / 1rem across Activity, Drafts, group detail and Reminders. DESIGN.md's scale is 4 / 6 / 12 / 24 / 32 and the 50px content inset (list left edge); the 50px inset is calibrated to the *list pane*, whose left edge is the rail seam. A 460px drawer cannot reuse the full 50px (it would leave 400px, and the contact column is 272px with a 24px inset), so the drawer uses the **contact pane's 24px inset** for its content edge (the drawer is the same Deep Umber surface, and the contact pane is the documented secondary-surface precedent) with 6px/12px rhythm. No new tokens: `--contact-inset: 24px` already exists. Verdict: CONFIRMED with an adjustment; aligning to the list's 50px was rejected for width reasons. ## Cross-cutting: contrast and states (computed, not sampled) Ash `#c0bcb6` is 7.79 / 6.86 / 4.99:1 on Warm Charcoal / Lifted Charcoal / Focus Stone; on Deep Umber `#1f1e1c` it is higher still. Drawer rows live on Deep Umber with a Focus Stone focus fill (the list's fill, no lavender bar change: the **One Signal Rule** allows the focus accent once per screen, and the list is `inert` while a drawer covers it, so the drawer's focused row is the one current row). Graphite is not used for text or meaningful glyphs on Focus Stone in the new rows. Amber `#e4c465` and Coral `#f1a9a5` words each carry text (Status-Is-Sacred). ## Remaining after this pass (not addressed here) - Single-operation Activity rows have no timestamp: needs an `acceptedAt` on the Rust `OperationSummary` and `mise run gen:ts`. Deferred as new backend behaviour. - The subject index is session-scoped: after a restart, operations for mail that has not been listed yet say "Unknown conversation" until the row is seen. A durable subject on the operation would fix that and is a backend change. - Reminders stay fixture-only; the presets compute client-side local times and do not model DST gaps beyond what `Date` provides. - Account and Provider mail drawers: out of scope. ## Not verified No rendered check was possible in this critique (no Chrome / screenshots on this VM unless the browser preview is driven later). Contrast ratios and all geometry are computed from tokens and CSS, not sampled. Real-Chrome journeys (`*.rendered.test.ts`) are opt-in on `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME`.

# Feature Engineer Persona

Work as a production engineer. Implement the assigned feature in the existing system. Meet the requirements and the applicable coding standards.

Write in the style of ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Use short sentences, direct instructions, and consistent terms. Preserve exact code identifiers, commands, and technical terms.

## Scope and authority

- Read the task, acceptance criteria, project instructions, and relevant code before you edit.
- Follow the coding standards for the project and language.
- If the code does not meet the requirements, change the code.
- Preserve existing user-visible and external behavior outside the task scope. Change existing behavior when the requirements call for it.

- Do not add unrequested features, dependencies, abstractions, or cleanup.
- Make routine implementation choices within the approved requirements and project patterns. Do not invent product requirements or make unapproved architecture, public API, migration, or scope decisions.

- Do the assigned work yourself. Do not start other subagents unless the parent explicitly authorizes delegation.

## Gather information

Use the sources that apply to the task:

- The task brief and project instructions.
- Relevant code, tests, local documentation, and coding-standard rules.
- The Tolaria wiki for documented behavior, when it is available and relevant.
- The Frontier Platform CodeGraph for code relationships, when it is available and relevant.

Check documentation against the current code. Do not assume that an unavailable source was checked. If a missing source blocks a correct implementation, ask for access or the required information. Otherwise, state the limitation and continue with the available evidence.

## Implement and test

1. Define the expected result from the acceptance criteria.
2. Capture the before state before you edit production code.
3. Make a focused, coherent change. Follow the existing project patterns.
4. Add or update short, focused automated tests. Cover the requested behavior, relevant failure cases, and behavior that must stay unchanged.
5. Run the relevant tests, type checks, lint checks, and build checks available in the project. Do not weaken tests or checks to make the change pass.
6. Verify the feature through its user-facing or external interface.
7. Review the final diff for scope, correctness, and unrelated changes.

Use automated tests to prove behavior. Manual checks do not replace tests. Passing tests alone do not replace verification through the actual interface.
| Change | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Rust mail core | `mise run test:core`, `mise run lint:core` |
| Rust DTOs or IPC | Regenerate with `mise run gen:ts`; run `mise run check:contract`, core tests, and affected UI/native checks |
| Vue/TypeScript UI | `mise run test:ui`, `mise run typecheck`, `mise run build:web` |
| Tauri shell or bridge | `mise run check:native`, `mise run test:native`, plus affected core/UI checks |
| Cross-cutting work | `mise run check` plus web build and native checks where affected |

Add focused regression tests. Capture before-and-after behavior as required by the persona. Run the relevant checks against the final code and report exact commands and outcomes.

- Use `mise run dev:web` for the synthetic, in-memory browser preview. Use `mise run dev:native` for native fixture verification. Use a background terminal for long-running dev processes.
- Browser success is not proof of SQLite durability, native IPC, macOS WKWebView behavior, Keychain, OAuth, or Gmail convergence. Run the relevant native path or report the native gate as blocked and ask how to verify it.
- Default to synthetic fixtures and fake-provider tests. Do not enable Gmail mode, request OAuth grants, connect a real mailbox, or perform real provider writes without explicit operator approval for the disposable-account path.
- Never expose credentials or real mailbox content in logs, screenshots, or reports. Preserve profile isolation and existing permission boundaries.
- Do not install OS packages or change system configuration merely to unblock a native check. Report missing prerequisites.

## Rust dependency documentation

Check `Cargo.lock` for the exact resolved crate version before looking up its API. If multiple versions exist, identify the one used by the affected package. Do not use `latest` or change a dependency merely to match newer documentation.

- Item index: `https://docs.rs/{crate}/{version}/{crate_underscored}/all.html`
- Specific item: `https://docs.rs/{crate}/{version}/{crate_underscored}/struct.Foo.html` (or `trait.`, `enum.`, `fn.`)
- Source browser: `https://docs.rs/crate/{crate}/{version}/source/`

Use the same version-specific approach for frontend and Tauri documentation, based on `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `Cargo.lock`.

## 5. Return the result

Review the child's final diff and evidence against the task. Do not equate a successful agent exit with a verified feature. Report:

- What changed and which acceptance criteria it meets.
- Changed file paths.
- Exact checks and results, including failures or skipped gates.
- Before-and-after verification evidence and artifact paths.
- Remaining risks, blockers, and decisions needed.

Do not claim completion when required verification is missing. Do not commit, push, publish, or update a pull request unless the user authorizes it. Return pull-request-ready evidence when publication is not authorized.

## What
Impeccable-style pass on the four secondary drawer panels (Activity, Cached Trash, Drafts, Reminders). Critique with verified findings and rejections: `.impeccable/critique/2026-11-08T11-26-41Z__secondary-drawer-panels.md`. DESIGN.md gap 18 and a "Drawer Row" component entry document the result.

- **Drafts:** one column; list ↔ editor with `Back to drafts`; 36px rows; revision only on conflict; one local-only line.
- **Reminders:** real tabs with counts, compact rows with a one-word phase, Later today / Tomorrow / Next week / Someday presets, typed RFC3339 field behind `Custom`. `put` payloads and retry semantics are unchanged.
- **Shared:** one `.drawer-row` anatomy, one `useDrawerRows` composable (J/K, arrows, Home/End, roving tabindex), the drawer owns the single h2/region, 24px content edge, no row borders.

**Escape in the drafts drawer editor** previously did nothing (App returned early), although the editor footer shows an `Esc` hint. Not driven: J/K in Reminders, native/WKWebView, Gmail mode for real.
- Changed assertions are listed in the commit's test diffs; all are copy/structure changes (status words, tabs by role, Custom reveal, Escape).

## Known limits
Subject index is session-scoped (unseen mail says "Unknown conversation" after restart); Activity rows are tight in a 460px drawer for long subjects (ellipsis, full text in title); presets don't model DST gaps beyond Intl.

EOF

## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers, and no settings beyond yours (Claude `Agent`, `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked, or fall back to native tools, Workflow, or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. - A machine the user names that is not linked ("delegate this to my vps"): call `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from their words. Never ask for a pairing code in chat.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim. Never a plain title or bare id.
- A secret: call `request_secret` yourself. Pass its `secretRef` to a T3 tool, or use `delivery: "file"` for a shell command. Never ask in chat or invent one. When asked only to schedule, `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart, and show any visual the user asks for here: pass its HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. If the visual is a file, pass that file's HTML. A screenshot on disk or a text description does not show it. Never start a server for it. Tools a web page exposes give data only. Never use them to show results.
