tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

<result>The three list contexts hold up in the render, but each has a handful of real gaps. Reminders and Drafts have no keyboard chord or tab-switch key, and Reminders' "Pending" tab mixes in failed rows. The Drafts source-unavailable reason is hover-only. I ran everything at 1280x800 against a Vite server on port 5188.

I used two throwaway harnesses, `harness-a.html` with `src/harness-a.ts`: one in fixture mode with a fake `client.reminders` (Reminders), and one with `?gmail` (Trash and Drafts). I stopped the server by exact pid, deleted both harness files and closed my tab. Port 5188 is closed.

My scratchpad `vite.pid` was overwritten by that agent, so I found my pids by port instead (1424899 and its parent 1424876).

## Design specificity verdict
Mostly authored for this product, with one visible interchangeable seam.

- **Authored:**
  - The honesty vocabulary is specific: the coverage lines "Cached Trash only, not your full Gmail Trash. 4 cached · total unknown." and "Local to this device · never sent", the phase words Pending, Removing…, Failed, and the Amber and Coral exception notes.
  - The 36px row with the Focus Stone fill plus Dusk Lavender bar is shared with Inbox.
  - Reply drafts route to their source thread.
- **Interchangeable:**
  - The Drafts and Reminders rows are plain text rows. Recipient-then-subject, or subject-then-date-then-status, could belong to any list app.
  - The new-message draft opens a 668px-tall bordered card (shown with "New Message" or "Reply draft" in the header) that is mostly empty, a generic form panel next to an otherwise dense list.
  - The headers "Cached Trash | Inbox 14" and "Drafts | Inbox 18" look like two sibling tabs, which is a generic-nav reading.

## Nielsen heuristics (Operate surfaces, all 10 apply)

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | Phases are honest and distinct (Pending, Removing…, Failed, Returned). But "Pending 4" counts the failed and removing rows, so the tab count overstates what is pending. The Drafts fallback reason is only in a `title` (`ComposeCard.vue:115`). |
| 2 | Match with real world | 3 | Copy is terse and exact. The failed-row note "Removal or return failed, or a later mailbox action superseded this reminder" does not say which. Empty states read "No history reminders." (template `No {{ destination }} reminders`, `RemindersList.vue`). |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc and Back return to the exact row everywhere I tested. A reply draft takes two Escs to reach the list (composer closes, then reader closes); a new-message draft takes one. There is no discard from the Drafts list. |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 3 | Tab switches splits in Inbox (`App.vue:2081`) but just moves focus in Reminders. The "Inbox N" tab sits beside the context h1. Row actions are hover/focus-revealed (`style.css:1517-1531`), unlike Inbox's glyph. |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Trash read-only holds: `e` and `r` did nothing and no composer appeared. Cancel reminder runs with no confirmation, though it is reversible. |
| 6 | Recognition over recall | 2 | Reminders row actions show only on the current or hovered row. Reminder tabs are Tab-reachable only. Drafts rows show no body text, so two drafts to the same person are indistinguishable. Rail labels are icon-only. |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 2 | The only chords are G E and G H (`App.vue:1240`); `browsing-actions.ts:27,30` gives Trash and Drafts an empty shortcut. There is no key to switch Reminders tabs, and no key to Reschedule, Cancel or Discard from a row. J/K and Enter are good. |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 3 | One quiet coverage line per context. The contact pane is dead chrome: "No correspondent information is available." beside Reminders and Drafts. |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Open errors show above the rows, so drafts are never hidden. Retry and Inspect durable state exist. No Retry on a failed reminder row, only Cancel. |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | Explanations live in hover titles. Inert keys in Trash give no feedback. |
| **Total** | | **27/40** | Good, with real gaps. |

## Cognitive-load failures
- **Working memory:** the user has to remember that Drafts and Trash have no chord, that Tab means different things in Inbox and Reminders, and that Reminders tabs are reachable only by Shift+Tab to the header.
- **More than 4 options at once:** the open reschedule picker shows 5 time choices (Later today, Tomorrow, Next week, Someday, Custom), the condition select (2 options) and 2 buttons. A focused Reminders row shows Open, Reschedule and Cancel reminder.
- **Hidden affordances:** the Reminders row actions are invisible on non-current rows, so only row 1 shows them on entry.
- **Layout shift:** the in-flow picker is about 158px tall and pushes the rows down while the user is rescheduling one of them.
- **Chunking:** the Pending tab mixes pending, removing and failed rows.

## Emotional journey
- **Entry:** calm and quick. The ordinary rows are fast, and Back returns to the row you left.
- **Valley:** the failed reminder. It is in coral with no recovery affordance beyond "Cancel reminder", and it carries an ambiguous explanation.
- **Second valley:** a reply draft whose source is unavailable. The Amber line is clear, but the reason (retained snapshot, headers unverifiable) is hover-only.
- **Exit:** peak-end is fine for Trash and Drafts. For Reminders the ending is flat: you return and nothing confirms the reschedule landed beyond the row text.

## What is working
1. **Honest state is built into the row.** Phase words keep Pending, Removing…, Failed and Returned separate in color and wording, and a draft is never made unopenable.
2. **The shared machinery holds up.** On Esc, Trash returned focus to the exact row (`conversation-row-conv-05`). Drafts returned to the row I had opened, including after the reader round-trip, and Reminders returned to the Invoice row after the reader.
3. **Trash is read-only by design:** the reader note "Cached Trash — read only. Recovery is not available here; use your provider client." is plain and correct.

## Priority issues

**[P1] Reminders keyboard model has no way to change tabs from the list.**
- **Evidence:** `reminders.onTabKeydown` handles arrows only once a tab has focus (`useReminders.ts:95`). There is no list-level key, and Tab from a row moves into Reschedule (`App.vue:2081` applies split-switching only to inbox and saved).
- **Why it matters:** this is the product's keyboard-first core, and Returned and History are effectively mouse-only.
- **Fix:** list-level `[` and `]` (or `1`, `2`, `3`) for Reminders tabs; give Drafts and Trash G chords.
- **Command:** `/impeccable shape`, then `/impeccable harden`.

**[P1] Pending tab counts failed and removing rows.**
- **Evidence:** the render shows "Pending 4" with a Failed row and a Removing… row, and the history bucket holds only cancelled.
- **Why it matters:** the tab count overstates what is pending, which is against the honest-state principle.
- **Fix:** surface a distinct "Needs attention" count or section for failed and removing rows. Give the failed row a Retry or a clear single cause.
- **Command:** `/impeccable clarify`.

**[P2] Drafts rows are not triageable.**
- **Evidence:** a row is recipient, subject, a "Reply" word, and a time. Nothing shows body, size or save state. The reason a reply draft's source is unavailable is hover-only, and there is no row-level Discard.
- **Why it matters:** opening each draft to tell them apart is the opposite of triage.
- **Fix:** add a one-line quiet body preview as the row secondary. Expose the fallback reason as visible text. Offer a Discard row action behind the existing confirmation.
- **Command:** `/impeccable layout`, then `/impeccable clarify`.

**[P2] Header composition reads as two tabs.**
- **Evidence:** "Cached Trash | Inbox 14" and "Drafts | Inbox 18" render with the h1 styled like an active tab and a live Inbox tab beside it.
- **Why it matters:** Inbox 14 also falls as trash items are counted, which is confusing in context.
- **Fix:** hide the split nav in list contexts (Reminders already does) or drop the count.
- **Command:** `/impeccable quieter`.

**[P3] Inconsistent Esc behaviour and dead states.**
- **Evidence:**
  - The reply draft takes two Escs; the new-message card takes one.
  - After closing a compose card from the Inbox list, `document.activeElement` was `BODY`, not a row.
  - The contact pane says "No correspondent information is available." in Reminders and Drafts.
  - Keys that do nothing in Trash (`e`, `r`) give no feedback.
- **Fix:** make Esc symmetric, restore row focus, hide or fill the contact pane, and give a one-line inert-key notice.
- **Command:** `/impeccable polish`.

## Persona red flags
- **Alex (power user):** no chord for Drafts or Trash, no tab-switch key in Reminders, and no row keys for Reschedule, Cancel or Discard. The Tab model contradicts Inbox.
- **Sam (accessibility):**
  - The fallback reason is title-only, so keyboard and screen-reader users never see it.
  - Rows are a roving-tabindex list, which is fine.
  - Hidden row actions are Tab-reachable but invisible until focused (opacity 0, not `display: none`).
  - The contact pane's heading, "Focused conversation", is noise in these contexts.
- **Riley (stress tester):** the in-flow picker is the tallest element and shifts rows. Cancel executes immediately. A failed reminder has no retry, only cancel. Dead keys in Trash are silent.

## Minor observations
- The Reminders date column is a fixed 12em with full dates ("Tue 10 Nov 2026, 2:00 PM"), which is precise but wide, unlike the compact Inbox dates.
- The reader opened from Reminders does not show reminder state (due time, reschedule). The h1 still says "Reminders" over an unrelated subject.
- The new-message card is 668px tall for four fields.
- Focus lands in the To field of an existing draft that already has a recipient.
- The contact pane shows "Composing to ada@example.test ada@example.test" (name equals address).

## Provocative questions
- If a failed reminder is the one thing that needs the user, why does it live in a Pending tab?
- Is a row-level Discard (with confirmation) safe enough to make Drafts a real triage surface?
- Could Drafts and Reminders share a single "Needs attention" strip instead of each carrying its own error styling?

## Not verified
- Failed or unknown Reminders request recovery (retry exact request, inspect durable state). My fake `cancel` throws, but I did not exercise it.
- Draft lifecycle alerts (suspended editor, close-protection, subscription errors) were read but not rendered.
- Real Tauri and native-mode behaviour, and VoiceOver or screen-reader output.
- The Starred context (only Trash, Drafts and Reminders were reviewed).
- Contrast ratios (judged by eye, not measured).
- Behaviour with more than a dozen rows or long subjects (only 2 to 6 rows).
- The "one-frame list flash" on failed source load. I did not observe it, but I also did not frame-step.</result>

## Design Specificity Verdict

**LLM assessment (A, unanchored):** mostly authored for this product, with two interchangeable seams.
- **Authored:**
  - The honesty vocabulary: "Cached Trash only, not your full Gmail Trash. 4 cached · total unknown.", "Local to this device · never sent", and the Amber and Coral exception lines.
  - The shared 36px row with the Focus Stone fill and Dusk Lavender bar.
  - Reply drafts routing to their source thread.
- **Generic:** Drafts and Reminders rows are plain text rows (recipient, subject, time). The new-message card is 668px tall for four fields.

**Deterministic scan (B):** the `.vue` files and `src/components` returned zero findings. The CSS scan gave six hits, all in `src/assets/style.css`, none introduced by this work:
- **side-tab ×3 (lines 881, 1201, 2487):** the 4px Lavender bar on `.inbox-row.focused, .context-row.focused` (line 1201) is the app's single documented focus cue in DESIGN.md. It is a false positive for design intent. The other two are the search and command-palette highlights.
- **radius ×3 (lines 351, 840, 1237):** 2px and 3px radii sit outside the 0/4/6/10/full scale. They are real but outside these contexts.

**Visual overlays:** injection succeeded on Trash, Drafts and Reminders. It reported one `straggler`: "available." alone on the last line of `P.contact-unknown` ("No correspondent information is available."). That element is in the contact pane. It was unstable, since one rescan returned nothing.

The overlay was a transient `[Human]` tab, and the live server and tab are stopped and closed, so nothing is left to look at.

## Overall Impression
The shared machinery works. The list rows, keyboard model and Back-to-row all behave like Inbox, and honest state is built into the rows. Compared with the drawers, this is a clear step up. What lags is keyboard reach: Reminders and Drafts are the least reachable lists in a keyboard-first product. The single biggest opportunity is giving these three lists the same accelerators Inbox and Done have.

## What's Working
1. **Honest state sits in the row.** Pending, Removing…, Failed and Returned differ in wording and colour, and a draft is never made unopenable. B measured Coral at 7.69:1 on Pane and Ash at 7.79:1.
2. **One focus cue, one row height.** All 8 measured rows were 36px. The focused row has a single Lavender bar, and the earlier double ring on the Reminders row is gone.
3. **Trash is read-only throughout.** Row actions are absent and the reader says "Cached Trash — read only. Recovery is not available here; use your provider client."

## Priority Issues

**[P1] Reminders tabs and row actions have no keyboard path from the list.**
- **Evidence:** the tab arrows work only once a tab has focus (`useReminders.ts:95`), and Tab from a row goes into Reschedule. Only `G H` and `G E` exist as chords. Trash and Drafts have none.
- **Why it matters:** Returned and History are effectively mouse-only, in a keyboard-first product.
- **Fix:** list-level `[` / `]` (or `1`/`2`/`3`) for Reminders tabs, and `G` chords for Trash and Drafts. Add row keys for Reschedule, Cancel and Discard.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable shape`, then `/impeccable harden`.

**[P2] "Pending" holds failed and removing rows, and the count includes them.**
- **Evidence:** "Pending 4" included a Failed row and a Removing… row. The bucket rule is `useReminders.ts:51`. The failed row offers Cancel but no Retry.
- **Why it matters:** the one row that needs the user is hidden among calm ones, and the tab count overstates pending.
- **Fix:** count only truly pending rows. Show failed and removing rows first under a "Needs attention" label, or with a separate count. Name the cause in the failed note.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable clarify`.

**[P2] Drafts rows can't be triaged, and the fallback reason is hover-only.**
- **Evidence:** a row is recipient, subject, a "Reply" word and a time. The visible Amber line says only "Source conversation unavailable", and the reason is a `title`.
- **Why it matters:** two drafts to the same person look identical, and keyboard and screen-reader users never see why the source can't host the reply.
- **Fix:** show a quiet one-line body preview as the row secondary. Make the reason visible text. Add a Discard row action behind the existing confirmation.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable layout`, then `/impeccable clarify`.

**[P2] The header reads as two sibling tabs.**
- **Evidence:** "Cached Trash | Inbox 14" and "Drafts | Inbox 18" render the h1 like an active tab with a live Inbox tab beside it. B found that Inbox tab is a plain `button` with no `aria-current`. The count also keeps falling as trash is browsed.
- **Why it matters:** a count that is irrelevant to the current list sits next to the title. Reminders already hides the split nav.
- **Fix:** hide the split nav in Trash and Drafts, or drop the count.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable quieter`.

**[P3] Esc asymmetry, dead states and small targets.**
- **Evidence:**
  - A reply draft takes two Escs, a new-message card one.
  - After closing a compose card from Inbox, focus fell to `BODY`.
  - The contact pane shows "No correspondent information is available." beside Reminders and Drafts.
  - `e` and `r` in Trash are silent.
  - Reminders Reschedule and Cancel are 24px high, and the focused-row Ash is only 4.99:1.
- **Fix:** make Esc symmetric, restore row focus, hide the contact pane in these contexts, add a one-line inert-key notice, and use 28–32px targets.
- **Suggested command:** `/impeccable polish`.

## Persona Red Flags
**Alex (power user):** No chord for Drafts or Trash. Reminders tabs can't be switched from the list. Reschedule, Cancel and Discard have no keys. Tab means "switch split" in Inbox and "go to the next button" in Reminders.

**Sam (accessibility):** The fallback reason is title-only. Hidden row actions are Tab-reachable but sit at opacity 0 until focused. No rail item is current in Reminders. Elsewhere the semantics are sound: one h1 per view, a proper tablist, a roving tabindex, and `aria-current="page"` on rail items.

**Riley (stress tester):** The in-flow picker is about 158px tall and pushes rows down mid-edit. Cancel runs immediately, and a failed reminder offers no Retry. Dead keys in Trash give no feedback. Only 2–6 rows were tried, so long lists and long subjects are untested.

## Minor Observations

## Action Summary

Scope is the top 3 issues, plus hiding the "Inbox N" tab, which you chose separately. Items 4 and 5 (Esc symmetry, focus after card close, contact pane, 24px targets) are out of scope.

1. **`/impeccable shape`, then `/impeccable harden` (P1, keyboard reach).**
   - Add list-level `[` and `]` to switch Reminders tabs.
   - Add `G` chords for Trash and Drafts. `G E` and `G H` exist today.
   - Add row keys for Reschedule, Cancel and Discard, and surface them in the command palette and hints.
   - Keep the editable/IME shortcut protection and the `G` hint line accurate.
2. **`/impeccable clarify` (P2, honest Reminders state).**
   - Count only truly pending reminders in the Pending tab.
   - Put failed and removing rows first under a "Needs attention" label, and name the failure cause in the failed note.
   - Add Retry on a failed reminder using the existing exact-request retry logic. This adds no backend behaviour.
3. **`/impeccable layout`, then `/impeccable clarify` (P2, Drafts triage).**
   - Add a one-line quiet body preview as the row secondary.
   - Make the "Source conversation unavailable" reason visible text, not just a `title`.
   - Add a Discard row action behind the existing confirmation. Drafts stay local-only.
4. **`/impeccable quieter` (header tab).** Hide the split nav in Trash and Drafts, as Reminders already does. Back and Esc still return to Inbox.
5. **`/impeccable polish`.** Final pass over the above.

You can ask me to run these one at a time, all at once, or in any order you prefer.

Re-run `/impeccable critique` after fixes to see your score improve.
